descripcion: At B2 a story is told with correct time sequencing: past simple for the main events, past perfect for whatever happened earlier. The dramaturgy of a C1 story (a hooked opening, a marked turning point) isn't the focus yet — getting the timeline clear is.

filas: We left early and missed the bus.
We'd already missed the train before we even got there.
It was raining when we arrived.

ejemplos.texto: We left early, but we'd already missed the connection.
It was raining heavily when we finally got there.
First we waited, then we just decided to walk.

notas: The past perfect marks what happened BEFORE the main story timeline — without it, the order of events can be unclear.
First, then, after that structure the story in time without needing extra tenses.
The past continuous is useful for background: what was going on when the main event happened.

contraste.es: El español tiene el pretérito pluscuamperfecto con la misma lógica, así que el concepto se transfiere fácilmente. La elección entre pretérito y pretérito perfecto en español sigue reglas distintas de las del inglés, que se basa más en si el tiempo está cerrado o no.

errores: Leaving out the past perfect, which makes the order of events unclear.
Using only the past simple throughout, even for events that happened earlier.
Using first, then and after that in the wrong order.
autochequeo: Is the earlier event marked with the past perfect where needed?
Is the past continuous used for background, not the main events?
Is the time order of the story clear?
Is the story more than just a list of events?
Have I used at least one past perfect correctly?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the time sequencing: past simple, past continuous, past perfect. Check whether earlier events are correctly marked. Do not rewrite the text.
